name: Mole brown
lede: Mole brown is a muted, warm grey-brown named for the animal's coat, listed by Ridgway in 1912 and matched in our own graph to the Japanese traditional grey Sunezumi, "plain mouse."

sections.title: A coat color, and a Japanese cousin
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature and the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 both carry this tone, though without a specific plate or block note in the records we hold [1]. In the ColorHub library the same point is also carried under Dark Vinaceous-Drab, an exact duplicate (ΔE 0.0) [1][3]. No book held in color-kb mentions "Mole brown" by name [4].

Its nearest distinct named neighbor, 2.7 units off and "almost the same" by our graph, is [[plain-mouse]], the English rendering of the Japanese traditional grey *Sunezumi* (素鼠) [3]. Edo-period Japan is recorded as naming dozens of distinct browns and greys for clothing; our graph's closest cross-reference for Mole brown among those traditional names is *Rikyu-nezumi*, 5.4 units off [3]. A fourth close cousin in the library is [[zinc-grey]], a cooler, greyer step away from the same point [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Mole brown in 1,441 of 23,781 paintings, about 6.1 percent, as photographed, making it one of the more common tones in this group [2]. It covers the largest share of canvas in East Asian works: a twelfth-century Chinese handscroll, [[painting:aic-96627|The Wangchuan Villa]], and a seventeenth-century Japanese screen by Kano Tan'yu, each over 85 percent [2]. Counts are computed matches on varnished, photographed paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
